1	// Splits shell command text the way a shell does, so a rule can tell a
2	// command that runs from text that only mentions one. Quoted text, heredoc
3	// bodies and arguments are data: only a word in command position counts as a
4	// command (`rg 'rm -rf'` and `git commit -m "... reset --hard"` are fine),
5	// while `bash -c "..."`, `$(...)` and backticks are looked into.
6	
7	/**
8	 * One simple command: its name (basename of the command word, after
9	 * assignments and wrappers such as `sudo`, `env`, `xargs`), its arguments
10	 * with quotes removed, and the files it redirects output into. `xargs` marks
11	 * a command run by xargs, whose operands come from its input.
12	 *
13	 * @typedef {{ name: string, args: string[], writes: string[], xargs?: boolean }} SimpleCommand
14	 */
15	
16	const SHELLS = new Set(['sh', 'bash', 'zsh', 'dash', 'ksh'])
17	const KEYWORDS = new Set(['!', '{', '}', 'if', 'then', 'else', 'elif', 'fi', 'do', 'done', 'while', 'until', 'time'])
18	
19	/** @param {string | undefined} w */
20	const base = w => (w ?? '').replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/').pop() ?? ''
21	
22	/**
23	 * Drops leading keywords, `VAR=value` assignments and wrapper commands, so
24	 * the first word left is the command that runs.
25	 *
26	 * @param {string[]} words
27	 */
28	function unwrap(words) {
29	  const w = [...words]
30	  /** @param {RegExp} [takesValue] */
31	  const dropFlags = takesValue => {
32	    while (w[0]?.startsWith('-')) {
33	      const f = /** @type {string} */ (w.shift())
34	      if (takesValue?.test(f)) w.shift()
35	    }
36	  }
37	  for (;;) {
38	    while (w.length && (KEYWORDS.has(/** @type {string} */ (w[0])) || /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\+?=/.test(/** @type {string} */ (w[0])))) w.shift()
39	    const name = base(w[0])
40	    if (name === 'env') {
41	      w.shift()
42	      while (w[0] !== undefined && (w[0].startsWith('-') || w[0].includes('='))) {
43	        const f = w.shift()
44	        if (f === '-u' || f === '-C') w.shift()
45	      }
46	    } else if (name === 'sudo' || name === 'doas') {
47	      w.shift()
48	      dropFlags(/^-[ugCDhpRrTt]$/)
49	    } else if (['command', 'exec', 'nohup', 'builtin', 'noglob', 'time'].includes(name)) {
50	      w.shift()
51	      dropFlags()
52	    } else if (name === 'nice') {
53	      w.shift()
54	      dropFlags(/^-n$/)
55	    } else if (name === 'timeout') {
56	      w.shift()
57	      dropFlags(/^(?:-s|-k|--signal|--kill-after)$/)
58	      w.shift() // the duration
59	    } else if (name === 'xargs') {
60	      w.shift()
61	      dropFlags(/^-[IdEnLPsa]$/)
62	    } else return w
63	  }
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Index of the `)` closing the `(` at `open`, skipping quoted text.
68	 *
69	 * @param {string} src
70	 * @param {number} open
71	 */
72	function closingParen(src, open) {
73	  let depth = 0
74	  for (let j = open; j < src.length; j++) {
75	    const c = src[j]
76	    if (c === '\\') j++
77	    else if (c === "'") {
78	      const k = src.indexOf("'", j + 1)
79	      j = k < 0 ? src.length : k
80	    } else if (c === '"') {
81	      for (j++; j < src.length && src[j] !== '"'; j++) if (src[j] === '\\') j++
82	    } else if (c === '(') depth++
83	    else if (c === ')' && --depth === 0) return j
84	  }
85	  return src.length
86	}
87	
88	/** @param {string} src @param {number} from index after the opening backtick */
89	function closingBacktick(src, from) {
90	  for (let j = from; j < src.length; j++) {
91	    if (src[j] === '\\') j++
92	    else if (src[j] === '`') return j
93	  }
94	  return src.length
95	}
96	
97	// Unquoted `{`, `,` and `}` while a word is read, so brace expansion can
98	// tell them from quoted ones.
99	const LB = ''
100	const CM = ''
101	const RB = ''
102	const BRACE_CHARS = { [LB]: '{', [CM]: ',', [RB]: '}' }
103	
104	/**
105	 * The words a word brace-expands to, as bash and zsh expand it
106	 * (`a{b,c}d` is `abd acd`; `{}` and `{x}` stay as they are).
107	 *
108	 * @param {string} w a word with its unquoted braces and commas marked
109	 * @returns {string[]}
110	 */
111	function expandBraces(w) {
112	  for (let i = w.indexOf(LB); i >= 0; i = w.indexOf(LB, i + 1)) {
113	    let depth = 0
114	    let close = -1
115	    const commas = []
116	    for (let j = i + 1; j < w.length && close < 0; j++) {
117	      if (w[j] === LB) depth++
118	      else if (w[j] === RB) {
119	        if (depth === 0) close = j
120	        else depth--
121	      } else if (w[j] === CM && depth === 0) commas.push(j)
122	    }
123	    if (close < 0 || !commas.length) continue
124	    const out = []
125	    let from = i + 1
126	    for (const k of [...commas, close]) {
127	      for (const x of expandBraces(w.slice(0, i) + w.slice(from, k) + w.slice(close + 1))) if (out.length < 64) out.push(x)
128	      from = k + 1
129	    }
130	    return out
131	  }
132	  return [w.replace(/[-]/g, ch => BRACE_CHARS[/** @type {keyof typeof BRACE_CHARS} */ (ch)])]
133	}
134	
135	/**
136	 * Splits a shell command line into simple commands, including the ones
137	 * inside `$(...)`, backticks, `<(...)`, `sh -c "..."`, `eval` and heredocs
138	 * fed to a shell. Heredoc bodies fed to anything else are data.
139	 *
140	 * @param {string} src
141	 * @param {number} [depth]
142	 * @returns {SimpleCommand[]}
143	 */
144	export function parseCommands(src, depth = 0) {
145	  /** @type {SimpleCommand[]} */
146	  const out = []
147	  if (depth > 6) return out
148	  const nested = (/** @type {string} */ s) => {
149	    for (const c of parseCommands(s, depth + 1)) out.push(c)
150	  }
151	
152	  /** @type {string[]} */
153	  let words = []
154	  /** @type {string[]} */
155	  let writes = []
156	  /** @type {string | null} */
157	  let word = null
158	  /** `dup`: after `>&`, where a descriptor number or `-` names no file. @type {'write' | 'dup' | 'read' | null} */
159	  let redirect = null
160	  /** @type {{ delim: string, strip: boolean, words: string[] }[]} */
161	  let heredocs = []
162	
163	  const append = (/** @type {string} */ s) => {
164	    word = (word ?? '') + s
165	  }
166	  const endWord = () => {
167	    if (word === null) return
168	    const expanded = expandBraces(word)
169	    if (redirect === 'write' || (redirect === 'dup' && !/^(?:\d+-?|-)$/.test(word))) writes.push(...expanded)
170	    else if (redirect !== 'read' && redirect !== 'dup') words.push(...expanded)
171	    redirect = null
172	    word = null
173	  }
174	  const endCommand = () => {
175	    endWord()
176	    redirect = null
177	    if (words.length || writes.length) {
178	      const w = unwrap(words)
179	      const name = base(w[0])
180	      const args = w.slice(1)
181	      const xargs = words.slice(0, words.length - w.length).some(x => base(x) === 'xargs')
182	      out.push(xargs ? { name, args, writes, xargs } : { name, args, writes })
183	      if (SHELLS.has(name)) {
184	        const c = args.findIndex(a => /^-[a-zA-Z]*c[a-zA-Z]*$/.test(a))
185	        if (c >= 0 && args[c + 1] !== undefined) nested(/** @type {string} */ (args[c + 1]))
186	      } else if (name === 'eval') nested(args.join(' '))
187	    }
188	    words = []
189	    writes = []
190	  }
191	
192	  const n = src.length
193	  let i = 0
194	  while (i < n) {
195	    const c = /** @type {string} */ (src[i])
196	    if (c === '\n') {
197	      const pending = heredocs
198	      endCommand()
199	      i++
200	      for (const h of pending) {
201	        /** @type {string[]} */
202	        const body = []
203	        while (i < n) {
204	          const e = src.indexOf('\n', i)
205	          const line = src.slice(i, e < 0 ? n : e)
206	          i = e < 0 ? n : e + 1
207	          if ((h.strip ? line.replace(/^\t+/, '') : line) === h.delim) break
208	          body.push(line)
209	        }
210	        // A heredoc fed to a shell is a script; fed to anything else it is data.
211	        if (SHELLS.has(base(unwrap(h.words)[0]))) nested(body.join('\n'))
212	      }
213	      heredocs = []
214	      continue
215	    }
216	    if (c === ' ' || c === '\t' || c === '\r') {
217	      endWord()
218	      i++
219	    } else if (c === '#' && word === null) {
220	      while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') i++
221	    } else if (c === '\\') {
222	      if (src[i + 1] !== '\n') append(src[i + 1] ?? '')
223	      i += 2
224	    } else if (c === "'") {
225	      const j = src.indexOf("'", i + 1)
226	      const end = j < 0 ? n : j
227	      append(src.slice(i + 1, end))
228	      i = end + 1
229	    } else if (c === '"') {
230	      append('')
231	      let j = i + 1
232	      for (; j < n && src[j] !== '"'; j++) {
233	        const d = src[j]
234	        if (d === '\\') {
235	          const e = src[j + 1] ?? ''
236	          if ('$`"\\'.includes(e)) append(e)
237	          else if (e !== '\n') append(`\\${e}`)
238	          j++
239	        } else if (d === '$' && src[j + 1] === '(') {
240	          const k = closingParen(src, j + 1)
241	          nested(src.slice(j + 2, k))
242	          append(src.slice(j, k + 1))
243	          j = k
244	        } else if (d === '`') {
245	          const k = closingBacktick(src, j + 1)
246	          nested(src.slice(j + 1, k))
247	          append(src.slice(j, k + 1))
248	          j = k
249	        } else append(/** @type {string} */ (d))
250	      }
251	      i = j + 1
252	    } else if (c === '`') {
253	      const k = closingBacktick(src, i + 1)
254	      nested(src.slice(i + 1, k))
255	      append(src.slice(i, k + 1))
256	      i = k + 1
257	    } else if ((c === '$' || c === '<' || c === '>') && src[i + 1] === '(') {
258	      // $(...) runs a command; <(...) and >(...) too, and stand for a path.
259	      const k = closingParen(src, i + 1)
260	      nested(src.slice(i + 2, k))
261	      append(src.slice(i, k + 1))
262	      i = k + 1
263	    } else if (c === ';' || c === '|' || c === '(' || c === ')') {
264	      endCommand()
265	      i++
266	    } else if (c === '&') {
267	      if (src[i + 1] === '>') {
268	        endWord()
269	        redirect = 'write'
270	        i += src[i + 2] === '>' ? 3 : 2
271	      } else {
272	        endCommand()
273	        i++
274	      }
275	    } else if (c === '>' || c === '<') {
276	      // A file descriptor number written right before the operator is part of it.
277	      if (word !== null && /^\d+$/.test(word)) word = null
278	      endWord()
279	      if (c === '<' && src[i + 1] === '<' && src[i + 2] === '<') {
280	        redirect = 'read' // here-string: the next word is input
281	        i += 3
282	      } else if (c === '<' && src[i + 1] === '<') {
283	        let j = i + 2
284	        const strip = src[j] === '-'
285	        if (strip) j++
286	        while (src[j] === ' ' || src[j] === '\t') j++
287	        let delim = ''
288	        while (j < n && !/[\s;&|<>()]/.test(/** @type {string} */ (src[j]))) delim += src[j++]
289	        heredocs.push({ delim: delim.replace(/["'\\]/g, ''), strip, words: [...words] })
290	        i = j
291	      } else if (c === '<') {
292	        redirect = src[i + 1] === '>' ? 'write' : 'read'
293	        i += src[i + 1] === '>' || src[i + 1] === '&' ? 2 : 1
294	      } else {
295	        let k = i + 1
296	        if (src[k] === '>' || src[k] === '|') k++
297	        redirect = src[k] === '&' ? 'dup' : 'write'
298	        if (src[k] === '&') k++
299	        i = k
300	      }
301	    } else {
302	      // `${...}` is a parameter, not a brace expansion.
303	      append(c === '{' && !(word ?? '').endsWith('$') ? LB : c === ',' ? CM : c === '}' ? RB : c)
304	      i++
305	    }
306	  }
307	  endCommand()
308	  return out
309	}

1	// The guard: the hard block on commands that destroy work or history.
2	//
3	// It reads command text, so it is a seatbelt, not a sandbox: aliases,
4	// functions and scripts can get past it.
5	
6	import { parseCommands } from './shell.mjs'
7	
8	/** @typedef {import('./shell.mjs').SimpleCommand} SimpleCommand */
9	
10	/** @param {string[]} args the arguments before a `--` */
11	const beforeDashDash = args => {
12	  const k = args.indexOf('--')
13	  return k < 0 ? args : args.slice(0, k)
14	}
15	
16	/**
17	 * The single-letter options set in `args` (clusters like `-fdx` included).
18	 * A letter in `valueLetters` takes the rest of its cluster, or the next
19	 * argument, as its value.
20	 *
21	 * @param {string[]} args
22	 * @param {string} [valueLetters]
23	 */
24	function shortFlags(args, valueLetters = '') {
25	  const set = new Set()
26	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
27	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
28	    if (!/^-[A-Za-z]+$/.test(a)) continue
29	    for (let j = 1; j < a.length; j++) {
30	      const ch = /** @type {string} */ (a[j])
31	      set.add(ch)
32	      if (valueLetters.includes(ch)) {
33	        if (j === a.length - 1) i++
34	        break
35	      }
36	    }
37	  }
38	  return set
39	}
40	
41	/**
42	 * Operands (non-option arguments), skipping the values of `valueOpts`.
43	 *
44	 * @param {string[]} args
45	 * @param {string[]} [valueOpts]
46	 */
47	function operands(args, valueOpts = []) {
48	  const out = []
49	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
50	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
51	    if (a === '--') return [...out, ...args.slice(i + 1)]
52	    if (valueOpts.includes(a)) i++
53	    else if (!a.startsWith('-') || a === '-') out.push(a)
54	  }
55	  return out
56	}
57	
58	const GIT_VALUE_OPTS = new Set(['-C', '-c', '--git-dir', '--work-tree', '--namespace', '--super-prefix', '--config-env'])
59	
60	/**
61	 * A git invocation split into its `-c` settings, its subcommand and the
62	 * subcommand's arguments.
63	 *
64	 * @param {string[]} args
65	 */
66	function gitParts(args) {
67	  /** @type {string[]} */
68	  const config = []
69	  let i = 0
70	  while (i < args.length && /** @type {string} */ (args[i]).startsWith('-')) {
71	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
72	    if (GIT_VALUE_OPTS.has(a)) {
73	      if (a === '-c' || a === '--config-env') config.push(args[i + 1] ?? '')
74	      i += 2
75	    } else {
76	      if (a.startsWith('--config-env=')) config.push(a.slice('--config-env='.length))
77	      i++
78	    }
79	  }
80	  const rest = args.slice(i + 1)
81	  const opts = beforeDashDash(rest)
82	  return { config, sub: args[i], rest, opts, long: (/** @type {string} */ f) => opts.some(x => x === f || x.startsWith(`${f}=`)) }
83	}
84	
85	/** @param {string[]} args */
86	function gitDestructive(args) {
87	  const { config, sub, rest, opts, long } = gitParts(args)
88	
89	  if (['commit', 'push', 'merge', 'rebase', 'am', 'cherry-pick', 'revert'].includes(sub ?? '')) {
90	    if (long('--no-verify')) return '--no-verify skips the repository checks'
91	    if (config.some(c => /^core\.hookspath\b/i.test(c))) return 'overriding core.hooksPath skips the repository checks'
92	  }
93	  switch (sub) {
94	    case 'reset':
95	      if (long('--hard')) return 'git reset --hard discards uncommitted work'
96	      break
97	    case 'clean': {
98	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'e')
99	      if ((s.has('f') || long('--force')) && !(s.has('n') || long('--dry-run'))) return 'git clean -f deletes untracked files'
100	      break
101	    }
102	    case 'checkout': {
103	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'bB')
104	      if (s.has('f') || long('--force')) return 'git checkout -f discards working-tree changes'
105	      const dd = rest.indexOf('--')
106	      if (dd >= 0 && dd < rest.length - 1) return 'git checkout [<ref>] -- <path> discards working-tree changes'
107	      const ops = operands(opts, ['-b', '-B', '--orphan'])
108	      if (ops.includes('.')) return 'git checkout . discards working-tree changes'
109	      const creates = s.has('b') || s.has('B') || long('--orphan')
110	      if (!creates && ops.length >= 2) return 'git checkout <ref> <path> overwrites working-tree files'
111	      break
112	    }
113	    case 'switch': {
114	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'cC')
115	      if (s.has('f') || long('--force') || long('--discard-changes')) return 'git switch --discard-changes discards working-tree changes'
116	      break
117	    }
118	    case 'restore': {
119	      // It only unstages with --staged and without --worktree.
120	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 's')
121	      const staged = s.has('S') || long('--staged')
122	      const worktree = s.has('W') || long('--worktree')
123	      if (!staged || worktree) return 'git restore discards working-tree changes'
124	      break
125	    }
126	    case 'push': {
127	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'o')
128	      if (s.has('f') || long('--force') || long('--force-with-lease') || long('--force-if-includes')) return 'force push rewrites shared history'
129	      if (operands(opts, ['-o', '--push-option', '--repo', '--receive-pack', '--exec']).some(x => x.startsWith('+'))) return 'a +refspec force-pushes'
130	      break
131	    }
132	    case 'stash':
133	      if (rest[0] === 'drop' || rest[0] === 'clear') return 'dropping a stash loses work'
134	      break
135	    case 'branch': {
136	      const s = shortFlags(opts)
137	      if (s.has('D') || ((s.has('d') || long('--delete')) && (s.has('f') || long('--force')))) return 'git branch -D deletes unmerged work'
138	      break
139	    }
140	    case 'commit': {
141	      if (shortFlags(opts, 'mFcCt').has('n')) return 'git commit -n skips the repository checks'
142	      break
143	    }
144	  }
145	  return null
146	}
147	
148	/**
149	 * @param {SimpleCommand} c
150	 * @returns {string | null} why the command is destructive
151	 */
152	function destructive(c) {
153	  if (c.name === 'git') return gitDestructive(c.args)
154	  if (c.name === 'rm') {
155	    const opts = beforeDashDash(c.args)
156	    if (shortFlags(opts).has('r') || shortFlags(opts).has('R') || opts.includes('--recursive')) return 'rm -r deletes whole directory trees'
157	  }
158	  return null
159	}
160	
161	/**
162	 * Why a shell command would destroy work or history, or null if it would not.
163	 *
164	 * @param {string} command
165	 * @returns {string | null}
166	 */
167	export function guard(command) {
168	  for (const c of parseCommands(command)) {
169	    const why = destructive(c)
170	    if (why) return why
171	  }
172	  return null
173	}

1	# cc-agents
2	
3	This repository ships **trace**, a Claude Code plugin that keeps a model's work tied to the reason for it and to the project's decisions.
4	
5	## The trace
6	
7	**Trace**:
8	The chain of records that ties a change to its reason: an issue, its branch, its commits, its pull request, and the progress comments on the issue.
9	_Avoid_: audit trail, traceability chain
10	
11	**Pipeline step**:
12	One stage of producing a traced change. The steps are listed in ADR 0006.
13	_Avoid_: phase, stage
14	
15	**Traced repository**:
16	A repository whose owner has opted it in to the trace.
17	_Avoid_: enabled repo
18	
19	**Linked issue**:
20	The open issue that the current branch belongs to.
21	_Avoid_: current ticket
22	
23	**Ticket**:
24	An issue describing one vertical slice of work, under a parent issue.
25	_Avoid_: story
26	
27	**Parent issue**:
28	The issue that holds an effort's goal and decisions, whose tickets are its sub-issues.
29	_Avoid_: epic
30	
31	**Progress comment**:
32	A comment on the linked issue recording a round of work's progress, decisions and verification results.
33	_Avoid_: status update, round comment
34	
35	**Bypass**:
36	The human's switch for turning the trace off for a session.
37	_Avoid_: override, escape hatch
38	
39	## Doc authority
40	
41	**Related docs**:
42	The docs an agent must have read before it may change a file. Which docs these are is decided by ADR 0007, not by the agent.
43	_Avoid_: governing docs, authoritative docs, relevant docs
44	
45	**Full read**:
46	An agent's own read of every line of a file in its current form.
47	_Avoid_: skim, partial read
48	
49	**Stale read**:
50	A read of a file that has changed since it was read.
51	
52	**Active ADR**:
53	A decision record still in force.
54	
55	## Archive
56	
57	**Archive**:
58	The human's store of superseded docs, outside every agent's reach.
59	_Avoid_: attic, old docs, deprecated folder
60	
61	**Superseded**:
62	Replaced by a newer decision.
63	_Avoid_: deprecated, obsolete
64	
65	## Guardrails and view
66	
67	**Hard block**:
68	A refusal of an agent's tool call, which the agent cannot proceed past.
69	_Avoid_: warning, notice
70	
71	**Nudge**:
72	A hard block that applies once, and lets the next attempt through.
73	
74	**Guard**:
75	The hard block on commands that destroy work or history.
76	_Avoid_: safety hook, git guard
77	
78	**Archive block**:
79	The hard block on agents touching the archive.
80	
81	**Band**:
82	The plugin's at-a-glance view of the trace.
83	_Avoid_: status bar
84

1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0005: Reuse existing skills and Claude Code; the plugin is guardrails and visibility only
8	
9	The quality-loop plugin grew to about 8.7k lines of Node. Most of it reimplemented review, fix and debug loops that Matt Pocock's skills and Claude Code's own tools now provide; much of the rest defended the loop's own state against the model. We replace it with a plugin, `trace`, that adds only what no existing tool does: hooks that enforce the trace and doc authority (ADRs 0006–0008), the guard on commands that destroy work or history, and a mod that shows the trace: the band and a `/trace` command.
10	
11	The work itself goes through existing skills:
12	
13	| Need | Use |
14	|---|---|
15	| Plan, spec, tickets | Matt's `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets` |
16	| Build | Matt's `implement`, `tdd` |
17	| Debug | Matt's `diagnosing-bugs` |
18	| Review | Claude Code's `/code-review` for bugs; Matt's `code-review` for standards and drift from the issue |
19	| PR body | Matt's `pr` |
20	| Orchestration | Claude Code's Workflow tool, not custom agents |
21	
22	- `plugin.json` declares `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` as a dependency, so the reused skills are always present.
23	- The plugin ships two skills. `trace` is model-invokable and maps the pipeline onto the skills above. `setup` is user-only. Skills stay short: they steer a capable model and do not script it.
24	- When sources disagree, Matt's skills and the claude.dev posts win over TStack. Nothing more is taken from TStack.
25	
26	Supersedes the archived ADRs "A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong", "A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike", "A second model reviews through GitHub Copilot CLI, as one more lens" and "full-send takes a finished loop to a merged PR, and merges on green CI".
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	- The old code is deleted, not archived, and nothing shims it. The git tag `quality-loop-v0.1.0` marks its last commit; `trace` starts at 0.2.0.
31	- A review step that votes on findings, as the old loop did, comes back only as a plugin `workflows/` script, and only once Claude Code's `/code-review` proves too noisy.
32

content:
1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0006: Every change is traced through GitHub, and hooks enforce it
8	
9	A change that cannot be tied to the reason it was made is how drift and hallucinated work get in. In a traced repository, every change follows one pipeline, the **trace**:
10	
11	1. **Read**: the related docs (ADR 0007).
12	2. **Track**: an issue describes the change; tickets come from `to-tickets`.
13	3. **Branch**: `gh issue develop <n>` creates `<n>-<slug>` from the latest default branch, or from its blocker's branch while the blocker's PR awaits merge.
14	4. **Implement**: commits reference `#<n>`.
15	5. **Review**: a PR whose body says `Closes #<n>`.
16	6. **Update**: a progress comment on the issue after each round, giving progress, decisions and verification results.
17	7. **Close**: the human merges, and `Closes #<n>` closes the issue. Work that is not merged is closed with GitHub's state reason and a comment.
18	
19	Hooks hard-block, in the main session and in every subagent:
20	- an edit on the default branch;
21	- an edit on a branch whose `<n>-` names no open issue;
22	- `git commit` without `#<n>`;
23	- `gh pr create` without `Closes #<n>`.
24	
25	When commits were pushed after the issue's last comment, the Stop hook nudges for a progress comment: it blocks stopping once. Every deny names the pipeline step to go back to.
26	
27	The issue is also the record that survives compaction. At start, after compaction, on resume and when a subagent starts, hooks inject the issue's title, acceptance criteria and latest progress comment.
28	
29	## Considered options
30	
31	- **A local task file** (the old loop's approach): rejected. It is invisible to humans, dies with the worktree, and duplicates the issue.
32	- **Merge automation on green CI**: rejected. Merging is the human's decision.
33	- **Notices instead of blocks**: rejected. A model can ignore a notice; it cannot ignore a deny.
34	
35	## Consequences
36	
37	- The trace applies only in repositories opted in by `/trace:setup`, and only to files inside that repository's working tree. The archive block and the guard apply everywhere.
38	- The only bypass is an environment variable the human sets when launching Claude Code. Nothing the model can write turns the trace off, so there is no state to defend.
39	- Because the human merges, a ticket blocked by an unmerged one is built on a stacked branch.
40	- Repositories without a GitHub remote cannot be traced.
41

1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0007: The related docs are forced reads, for every agent, before any edit
8	
9	Stale specs and invented terms enter when a model edits before it has read what the project already decided. Leaving the choice of what to read to the model means a relevant doc can be skipped. So the **related docs** are decided mechanically, and reading them is enforced:
10	
11	- `GLOSSARY.md`.
12	- The linked issue with its comments (`gh issue view <n> --comments`).
13	- Every active ADR in `docs/adr/`. An ADR may narrow itself with an `applies-to:` list of path globs in its frontmatter. It is then related only to edits of matching paths. An ADR without one is related to every edit.
14	- Every file under `docs/` that the issue body links.
15	
16	A doc counts as read only when the agent has read **the whole file itself**:
17	- Reads in chunks add up to the whole file.
18	- A partial view does not count.
19	- A read goes stale when the file's content changes after it.
20	- A subagent's reads are its own: its parent's context is not its context.
21	
22	A hard deny on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and on `git commit` as the backstop for changes made through Bash, lists exactly which docs are unread or stale. Where the hook's input is uncertain or undocumented, the check requires a re-read and never skips one.
23	
24	## Considered options
25	
26	- **The model chooses the relevant ADRs, with hooks only reminding it**: rejected by the user. A doc left to judgement is a doc that can be ignored.
27	- **Parsing every Bash command for writes**: rejected. That is what made the old guard 1,445 lines. The commit gate catches Bash-made changes before they land.
28	
29	## Consequences
30	
31	- Forced reads apply where the trace does: in traced repositories, to files inside the repository's working tree (ADR 0006).
32

1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0008: Superseded docs live in a human-only archive that no agent can read
8	
9	A superseded ADR or doc in the model's context is a stale spec it may follow. Deleting it loses the human's record. So superseded docs move to `archive/` at the repository root, mirroring their original paths, each with a one-line "Superseded by ADR-NNNN" header. Active docs name an archived doc by title, never by link.
10	
11	The archive is managed by the human alone. Every model and agent, subagents and workflow agents included, is hard-denied:
12	- reading, searching or listing inside it;
13	- editing, writing or deleting there;
14	- moving or copying anything out of it;
15	- Bash commands that read a path inside it.
16	
17	Moving a file **into** the archive is allowed.
18	
19	Enforcement has two layers. The plugin's PreToolUse hook applies in every repository, because plugins cannot ship permission rules. In traced repositories, `/trace:setup` also adds Claude Code's own `Read(./archive/**)` deny rule to project settings.
20	
21	## Considered options
22	
23	- **A SubagentStart notice or injected context telling agents to stay out**: rejected. A notice is not enforcement; only a deny is.
24	
25	## Consequences
26	
27	- The hook reads command text. A search that reaches the archive without naming it, such as a repository-wide `rg`, must still be denied. Any route that cannot be closed is recorded here with the reason.
28	- That the hook fires for Workflow agents and Claude Code's `/code-review` fork is still to be verified. Until it is, those agents are not counted as covered.
29	- Code is never archived. Git history and tags keep it, and archived code would be exactly the context this exists to keep out.
30

1	# trace
2	
3	Hooks that keep a model's work traced and its context grounded in the project's decisions (ADRs 0005–0008). It depends on `mattpocock-skills`, which supplies the skills the work goes through.
4	
5	## The guard
6	
7	A PreToolUse hook on Bash. In every repository, and in every subagent, it refuses commands that destroy work or history:
8	
9	- `git reset --hard`, `clean -f`, discarding checkouts, switches and restores
10	- force pushes, including `+refspec`
11	- `stash drop` / `clear`, `branch -D`
12	- `--no-verify`, `commit -n`, and overriding `core.hooksPath`
13	- `rm -r`
14	
15	It parses the command the way a shell does. Text that only mentions a command is allowed, such as `rg 'rm -rf'` or a commit message. Commands inside `bash -c`, `$(...)` and heredocs fed to a shell are checked. It reads command text, so it is a seatbelt, not a sandbox.
16	
17	## Compaction
18	
19	The trace keeps state in GitHub, not in the context. To compact earlier, at about 300k tokens for example, use Claude Code's own `autoCompactWindow` setting. The plugin does not manage compaction.

content:
Review target: `bfa09ae..HEAD`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

     2	// command that runs from text that only mentions one. Quoted text, heredoc

     5	// while `bash -c "..."`, `$(...)`, backticks and `find -exec` are looked into.

     9	 * assignments and wrappers such as `sudo`, `env`, `xargs`) and its arguments
    10	 * with quotes removed.
    11	 *
    12	 * @typedef {{ name: string, args: string[] }} SimpleCommand
    13	 */

    16	// Commands that run what they read from a heredoc or a pipe as a script.
    17	const SCRIPT_READERS = new Set([...SHELLS, 'source', '.'])
    18	// `find` actions that run a command, ended by `;` or `+`.
    19	const FIND_EXEC = new Set(['-exec', '-execdir', '-ok', '-okdir'])
    20	// Most words one word may brace-expand to.

    35	  /** @param {RegExp} [takesValue] */

content:
Review target: `3b62dc7..HEAD`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

   126	const ANSI_C_ESCAPES = /** @type {Record<string, string>} */ ({ a: '\x07', b: '\b', e: '\x1b', E: '\x1b', f: '\f', n: '\n', r: '\r', t: '\t', v: '\v' })
   127	
   128	/**
   129	 * The text an ANSI-C quoted string `$'...'` stands for, given what is between
   130	 * its quotes.
   131	 *
   132	 * @param {string} s
   133	 */
   134	function ansiC(s) {
   135	  return s.replace(/\\(?:x([0-9a-fA-F]{1,2})|u([0-9a-fA-F]{1,4})|U([0-9a-fA-F]{1,8})|([0-7]{1,3})|c([\s\S])|([\s\S]))/g, (_, x, u, U, o, c, e) => {
   136	    const code = x ?? u ?? U
   137	    if (code) return String.fromCodePoint(Math.min(parseInt(code, 16), 0x10ffff))
   138	    if (o) return String.fromCharCode(parseInt(o, 8) & 0xff)
   139	    if (c) return String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) & 0x1f)
   140	    return ANSI_C_ESCAPES[e] ?? ('\\\'"?'.includes(e) ? e : `\\${e}`)
   141	  })
   142	}
   143	
   144	// Unquoted `{`, `,` and `}` while a word is read, so brace expansion can
   145	// tell them from quoted ones.
   146	const LB = ''
   147	const CM = ''
   148	const RB = ''
   149	const BRACE_CHARS = { [LB]: '{', [CM]: ',', [RB]: '}' }
   150	
   200	    return [...out]
   201	  }
   202	  return [unmark(w)]
   203	}
   204	
   205	/**
   206	 * Splits a shell command line into simple commands, including the ones
   207	 * inside `$(...)`, backticks, `<(...)`, `sh -c "..."`, `eval`, `find -exec`
   208	 * and heredocs a shell may read. Heredoc bodies fed to anything else are data,
   209	 * apart from the substitutions in an unquoted one.
   210	 *
   211	 * @param {string} src
   212	 * @param {number} [depth]
   213	 * @returns {SimpleCommand[]}
   214	 */
   215	export function parseCommands(src, depth = 0) {
   216	  /** @type {SimpleCommand[]} */
   217	  const out = []
   218	  if (depth > 6) return out
   219	  const nested = (/** @type {string} */ s) => {
   220	    for (const c of parseCommands(s, depth + 1)) out.push(c)
   221	  }
   222	
   223	  /** @type {string[]} */
   224	  let words = []
   225	  /** @type {string | null} */
   226	  let word = null
   227	  /**
   228	   * What the next word is when it is not an argument: a redirection's target,
   229	   * or a here-string, which is the command's input.
   230	   * @type {'target' | 'here-string' | null}
   231	   */
   232	  let redirect = null
   233	  /** @type {string[]} */
   234	  let hereStrings = []
   235	  /**
   236	   * Heredocs whose bodies start after the next newline. `quoted`: the
   237	   * delimiter was quoted, so the body is not expanded. `pipeline`: the
   238	   * pipeline of the command it feeds.
   239	   * @type {{ delim: string, strip: boolean, quoted: boolean, pipeline: number }[]}
   240	   */
   241	  let heredocs = []
   242	  // The current pipeline, and the commands of every pipeline at this level.
   243	  let pipeline = 0
   244	  /** @type {(SimpleCommand & { pipeline: number })[]} */
   245	  const stages = []
   246	  // A `|` was read and the command after it has not been yet.
   247	  let openPipe = false
   248	
   249	  const append = (/** @type {string} */ s) => {
   250	    word = (word ?? '') + s
   251	  }
   252	  const endWord = () => {
   253	    if (word === null) return
   254	    if (redirect === 'here-string') hereStrings.push(word)
   255	    else if (!redirect) words.push(...expandBraces(word))
   256	    redirect = null
   257	    word = null
   258	  }
   259	  /**
   260	   * @param {string[]} cmdWords
   261	   * @param {string[]} input here-strings the command reads
   262	   */
   263	  const emit = (cmdWords, input = []) => {
   264	    const w = unwrap(cmdWords)
   265	    const name = base(w[0])
   266	    const args = w.slice(1)
   267	    out.push({ name, args })
   268	    if (SCRIPT_READERS.has(name)) for (const h of input) nested(h)
   269	    if (SHELLS.has(name)) {
   270	      const c = args.findIndex(a => /^-[a-zA-Z]*c[a-zA-Z]*$/.test(a))
   271	      if (c >= 0 && args[c + 1] !== undefined) nested(/** @type {string} */ (args[c + 1]))
   272	    } else if (name === 'eval') nested(args.join(' '))
   273	    else if (name === 'find') {
   274	      for (let k = 0; k < args.length; k++) {
   275	        if (!FIND_EXEC.has(/** @type {string} */ (args[k]))) continue
   276	        let end = k + 1
   277	        while (end < args.length && args[end] !== ';' && args[end] !== '+') end++
   278	        if (end > k + 1) emit(args.slice(k + 1, end))
   279	        k = end
   280	      }
   281	    }
   282	    return { name, args }
   283	  }
   284	  // When a shell reads a pipeline's output (`echo 'git reset --hard' | bash`),
   285	  // what echo and printf write is a script.
   286	  const endPipeline = () => {
   287	    const ps = stages.filter(st => st.pipeline === pipeline)
   288	    if (ps.some((st, k) => k > 0 && SCRIPT_READERS.has(st.name))) {
   289	      for (const st of ps) {
   290	        if (st.name !== 'echo' && st.name !== 'printf') continue
   291	        const text = st.args.filter(a => !/^-[neE]+$/.test(a))
   292	        nested(text.join(' '))
   293	        for (const a of text) nested(a)
   294	      }
   295	    }
   296	    pipeline++
   297	    openPipe = false
   298	  }
   299	  /** @param {'pipe' | 'end' | 'newline' | 'group'} sep what ends the command: `|`, a list operator, a newline, or a parenthesis */
   300	  const endCommand = sep => {
   301	    endWord()
   302	    redirect = null
   303	    if (words.length) {
   304	      stages.push({ ...emit(words, hereStrings), pipeline })
   305	      openPipe = false
   306	    }
   307	    words = []
   308	    hereStrings = []
   309	    if (sep === 'pipe') openPipe = true
   310	    else if (sep === 'end' || (sep === 'newline' && !openPipe)) endPipeline()
   311	  }
   312	
   313	  const n = src.length
   314	  let i = 0
   315	  while (i < n) {
   316	    const c = /** @type {string} */ (src[i])
   317	    if (c === '\n') {
   318	      const pending = heredocs
   319	      endCommand('newline')
   320	      i++
   321	      for (const h of pending) {
   322	        // A heredoc is a script when a shell in its pipeline may read it,
   323	        // directly (`bash <<EOF`) or through a pipe (`cat <<EOF | bash`), or
   324	        // when its pipeline goes on after the body, where that is unknown.
   325	        const script = (openPipe && h.pipeline === pipeline) || stages.some(st => st.pipeline === h.pipeline && SCRIPT_READERS.has(st.name))
   326	        /** @type {string[]} */
   327	        const body = []
   328	        while (i < n) {
   329	          const e = src.indexOf('\n', i)
   330	          const line = src.slice(i, e < 0 ? n : e)
   331	          i = e < 0 ? n : e + 1
   332	          if ((h.strip ? line.replace(/^\t+/, '') : line) === h.delim) break
   333	          body.push(line)
   334	        }
   335	        // Fed to anything else it is data, though an unquoted delimiter
   336	        // still runs the body's `$(...)` and backticks.
   337	        if (script) nested(body.join('\n'))
   338	        else if (!h.quoted) for (const s of substitutions(body.join('\n'))) nested(s)
   339	      }
   340	      heredocs = []
   341	      continue
   342	    }
   343	    if (c === ' ' || c === '\t' || c === '\r') {
   344	      endWord()
   345	      i++
   346	    } else if (c === '#' && word === null) {
   347	      while (i < n && src[i] !== '\n') i++
   348	    } else if (c === '\\') {
   349	      if (src[i + 1] !== '\n') append(src[i + 1] ?? '')
   350	      i += 2
   351	    } else if (c === '$' && src[i + 1] === "'") {
   352	      // ANSI-C quoting: `$'\x67it'` is `git`.
   353	      let j = i + 2
   354	      while (j < n && src[j] !== "'") j += src[j] === '\\' ? 2 : 1
   355	      append(ansiC(src.slice(i + 2, Math.min(j, n))))
   356	      i = j + 1
   357	    } else if (c === '$' && src[i + 1] === '"') {
   358	      // Locale quoting: `$"..."` reads as `"..."`.
   359	      i++
   360	    } else if (c === "'") {
   361	      const j = src.indexOf("'", i + 1)
   362	      const end = j < 0 ? n : j
   363	      append(src.slice(i + 1, end))
   364	      i = end + 1
   365	    } else if (c === '"') {
   366	      append('')
   367	      let j = i + 1
   368	      for (; j < n && src[j] !== '"'; j++) {
   369	        const d = src[j]
   370	        if (d === '\\') {
   371	          const e = src[j + 1] ?? ''
   372	          if ('$`"\\'.includes(e)) append(e)
   373	          else if (e !== '\n') append(`\\${e}`)
   374	          j++
   375	        } else if (d === '$' && src[j + 1] === '(') {
   376	          const k = closingParen(src, j + 1)
   377	          nested(src.slice(j + 2, k))
   378	          append(src.slice(j, k + 1))
   379	          j = k
   380	        } else if (d === '`') {
   381	          const k = closingBacktick(src, j + 1)
   382	          nested(src.slice(j + 1, k))
   383	          append(src.slice(j, k + 1))
   384	          j = k
   385	        } else append(/** @type {string} */ (d))
   386	      }
   387	      i = j + 1
   388	    } else if (c === '`') {
   389	      const k = closingBacktick(src, i + 1)
   390	      nested(src.slice(i + 1, k))
   391	      append(src.slice(i, k + 1))
   392	      i = k + 1
   393	    } else if ((c === '$' || c === '<' || c === '>') && src[i + 1] === '(') {
   394	      // $(...) runs a command; <(...) and >(...) too, and stand for a path.
   395	      const k = closingParen(src, i + 1)
   396	      nested(src.slice(i + 2, k))
   397	      append(src.slice(i, k + 1))
   398	      i = k + 1
   399	    } else if (c === '|') {
   400	      // `||` ends a pipeline; `|` and `|&` continue it.
   401	      endCommand(src[i + 1] === '|' ? 'end' : 'pipe')
   402	      i += src[i + 1] === '|' || src[i + 1] === '&' ? 2 : 1
   403	    } else if (c === ';') {
   404	      endCommand('end')
   405	      i++
   406	    } else if (c === '(' || c === ')') {
   407	      endCommand('group')
   408	      i++
   409	    } else if (c === '&') {
   410	      if (src[i + 1] === '>') {
   411	        endWord()
   412	        redirect = 'target'
   413	        i += src[i + 2] === '>' ? 3 : 2
   414	      } else {
   415	        endCommand('end')
   416	        i += src[i + 1] === '&' ? 2 : 1
   417	      }
   418	    } else if (c === '>' || c === '<') {
   419	      // A file descriptor number written right before the operator is part of it.
   420	      if (word !== null && /^\d+$/.test(word)) word = null
   421	      endWord()
   422	      if (c === '<' && src[i + 1] === '<' && src[i + 2] === '<') {
   423	        redirect = 'here-string'
   424	        i += 3
   425	      } else if (c === '<' && src[i + 1] === '<') {
   426	        let j = i + 2
   427	        const strip = src[j] === '-'
   428	        if (strip) j++
   429	        while (src[j] === ' ' || src[j] === '\t') j++
   430	        let delim = ''
   431	        while (j < n && !/[\s;&|<>()]/.test(/** @type {string} */ (src[j]))) delim += src[j++]
   432	        heredocs.push({ delim: delim.replace(/["'\\]/g, ''), strip, quoted: /["'\\]/.test(delim), pipeline })
   433	        i = j
   434	      } else if (c === '<') {
   435	        redirect = 'target'
   436	        i += src[i + 1] === '>' || src[i + 1] === '&' ? 2 : 1
   437	      } else {
   438	        let k = i + 1
   439	        if (src[k] === '>' || src[k] === '|') k++
   440	        if (src[k] === '&') k++
   441	        redirect = 'target'
   442	        i = k
   443	      }
   444	    } else {
   445	      // `${...}` is a parameter, not a brace expansion.
   446	      append(c === '{' && !(word ?? '').endsWith('$') ? LB : c === ',' ? CM : c === '}' ? RB : c)
   447	      i++
   448	    }
   449	  }
   450	  endCommand('end')
   451	  return out
   452	}

1	// The guard: the hard block on commands that destroy work or history.
     2	//
     3	// It reads command text, so it is a seatbelt, not a sandbox: aliases,
     4	// functions and scripts can get past it.
     5	
     6	import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'
     7	
     8	import { parseCommands } from './shell.mjs'
     9	
    10	/** @typedef {import('./shell.mjs').SimpleCommand} SimpleCommand */
    11	/**
    12	 * Whether a path, relative to the command's working directory, exists.
    13	 * Without one, every operand reads as a branch name.
    14	 *
    15	 * @typedef {(path: string) => boolean} IsPath
    16	 */
    17	
    18	/** @param {string[]} args the arguments before a `--` */
    19	const beforeDashDash = args => {
    20	  const k = args.indexOf('--')
    21	  return k < 0 ? args : args.slice(0, k)
    22	}
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * The single-letter options set in `args` (clusters like `-fdx` included).
    26	 * A letter in `valueLetters` takes the rest of its cluster, or the next
    27	 * argument, as its value.
    28	 *
    29	 * @param {string[]} args
    30	 * @param {string} [valueLetters]
    31	 */
    32	function shortFlags(args, valueLetters = '') {
    33	  const set = new Set()
    34	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    35	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
    36	    if (!/^-[A-Za-z]+$/.test(a)) continue
    37	    for (let j = 1; j < a.length; j++) {
    38	      const ch = /** @type {string} */ (a[j])
    39	      set.add(ch)
    40	      if (valueLetters.includes(ch)) {
    41	        if (j === a.length - 1) i++
    42	        break
    43	      }
    44	    }
    45	  }
    46	  return set
    47	}
    48	
    49	/**
    50	 * Operands (non-option arguments), skipping the values of `valueOpts`.
    51	 *
    52	 * @param {string[]} args
    53	 * @param {string[]} [valueOpts]
    54	 */
    55	function operands(args, valueOpts = []) {
    56	  const out = []
    57	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    58	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
    59	    if (a === '--') return [...out, ...args.slice(i + 1)]
    60	    if (valueOpts.includes(a)) i++
    61	    else if (!a.startsWith('-') || a === '-') out.push(a)
    62	  }
    63	  return out
    64	}
    65	
    66	const GIT_VALUE_OPTS = new Set(['-C', '-c', '--git-dir', '--work-tree', '--namespace', '--super-prefix', '--config-env'])
    67	
    68	/**
    69	 * A git invocation split into its `-c` settings, its `-C` directories, its
    70	 * subcommand and the subcommand's arguments.
    71	 *
    72	 * @param {string[]} args
    73	 */
    74	function gitParts(args) {
    75	  /** @type {string[]} */
    76	  const config = []
    77	  /** @type {string[]} */
    78	  const dirs = []
    79	  let i = 0
    80	  while (i < args.length && /** @type {string} */ (args[i]).startsWith('-')) {
    81	    const a = /** @type {string} */ (args[i])
    82	    if (GIT_VALUE_OPTS.has(a)) {
    83	      if (a === '-c' || a === '--config-env') config.push(args[i + 1] ?? '')
    84	      if (a === '-C') dirs.push(args[i + 1] ?? '.')
    85	      i += 2
    86	    } else {
    87	      if (a.startsWith('--config-env=')) config.push(a.slice('--config-env='.length))
    88	      i++
    89	    }
    90	  }
    91	  const rest = args.slice(i + 1)
    92	  const opts = beforeDashDash(rest)
    93	  return { config, dirs, sub: args[i], rest, opts, hasLong: (/** @type {string} */ f) => opts.some(x => x === f || x.startsWith(`${f}=`)) }
    94	}
    95	
    96	/**
    97	 * @param {string[]} args
    98	 * @param {IsPath} isPath
    99	 */
   100	function gitDestructive(args, isPath) {
   101	  const { config, dirs, sub, rest, opts, hasLong } = gitParts(args)
   102	
   103	  if (['commit', 'push', 'merge', 'rebase', 'am', 'cherry-pick', 'revert'].includes(sub ?? '')) {
   104	    if (hasLong('--no-verify')) return '--no-verify skips the repository checks'
   105	    if (config.some(c => /^core\.hookspath\b/i.test(c))) return 'overriding core.hooksPath skips the repository checks'
   106	  }
   107	  switch (sub) {
   108	    case 'reset':
   109	      if (hasLong('--hard')) return 'git reset --hard discards uncommitted work'
   110	      break
   111	    case 'clean': {
   112	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'e')
   113	      if ((s.has('f') || hasLong('--force')) && !(s.has('n') || hasLong('--dry-run'))) return 'git clean -f deletes untracked files'
   114	      break
   115	    }
   116	    case 'checkout': {
   117	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'bB')
   118	      if (s.has('f') || hasLong('--force')) return 'git checkout -f discards working-tree changes'
   119	      const dd = rest.indexOf('--')
   120	      if (dd >= 0 && dd < rest.length - 1) return 'git checkout [<ref>] -- <path> discards working-tree changes'
   121	      const ops = operands(opts, ['-b', '-B', '--orphan'])
   122	      if (ops.includes('.')) return 'git checkout . discards working-tree changes'
   123	      const creates = s.has('b') || s.has('B') || hasLong('--orphan')
   124	      if (!creates && ops.length >= 2) return 'git checkout <ref> <path> overwrites working-tree files'
   125	      if (hasLong('--pathspec-from-file')) return 'git checkout --pathspec-from-file discards working-tree changes'
   126	      // `git checkout <x>` restores x when it is a path, and switches to it
   127	      // when it is a branch. A ref name cannot hold a glob or start with `:`,
   128	      // so those are pathspecs; otherwise only the filesystem can tell, and a
   129	      // name that is both is refused: `git switch` takes only branches.
   130	      const op = ops[0]
   131	      if (!creates && op !== undefined && (/[*?[]|^:/.test(op) || isPath(dirs.concat(op).reduce((a, b) => (isAbsolute(b) ? b : join(a, b))))))
   132	        return 'git checkout <path> discards working-tree changes; to switch branches, use git switch'
   133	      break
   134	    }
   135	    case 'switch': {
   136	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'cC')
   137	      if (s.has('f') || hasLong('--force') || hasLong('--discard-changes')) return 'git switch --discard-changes discards working-tree changes'
   138	      break
   139	    }
   140	    case 'restore': {
   141	      // It only unstages with --staged and without --worktree.
   142	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 's')
   143	      const staged = s.has('S') || hasLong('--staged')
   144	      const worktree = s.has('W') || hasLong('--worktree')
   145	      if (!staged || worktree) return 'git restore discards working-tree changes'
   146	      break
   147	    }
   148	    case 'push': {
   149	      const s = shortFlags(opts, 'o')
   150	      if (s.has('f') || hasLong('--force') || hasLong('--force-with-lease') || hasLong('--force-if-includes')) return 'force push rewrites shared history'
   151	      if (s.has('d') || hasLong('--delete')) return 'git push --delete deletes remote refs'
   152	      if (hasLong('--mirror') || hasLong('--prune')) return 'git push --mirror/--prune deletes remote refs'
   153	      const refspecs = operands(opts, ['-o', '--push-option', '--repo', '--receive-pack', '--exec'])
   154	      if (refspecs.some(x => x.startsWith('+'))) return 'a +refspec force-pushes'
   155	      if (refspecs.some(x => /^:./.test(x))) return 'a :refspec deletes a remote ref'
   156	      break
   157	    }
   158	    case 'stash': {
   159	      const action = operands(rest)[0]
   160	      if (action === 'drop' || action === 'clear') return 'dropping a stash loses work'
   161	      break
   162	    }
   163	    case 'branch': {
   164	      const s = shortFlags(opts)
   165	      if (s.has('D') || ((s.has('d') || hasLong('--delete')) && (s.has('f') || hasLong('--force')))) return 'git branch -D deletes unmerged work'
   166	      break
   167	    }
   168	    case 'commit': {
   169	      if (shortFlags(opts, 'mFcCt').has('n')) return 'git commit -n skips the repository checks'
   170	      break
   171	    }
   172	  }
   173	  return null
   174	}
   175	
   176	/**
   177	 * @param {SimpleCommand} c
   178	 * @param {IsPath} isPath
   179	 * @returns {string | null} why the command is destructive
   180	 */
   181	function destructive(c, isPath) {
   182	  if (c.name === 'git') return gitDestructive(c.args, isPath)
   183	  if (c.name === 'rm') {
   184	    const opts = beforeDashDash(c.args)
   185	    const s = shortFlags(opts)
   186	    if (s.has('r') || s.has('R') || opts.includes('--recursive')) return 'rm -r deletes whole directory trees'
   187	  }
   188	  return null
   189	}
   190	
   191	/**
   192	 * Why a shell command would destroy work or history, or null if it would not.
   193	 *
   194	 * @param {string} command
   195	 * @param {{ isPath?: IsPath }} [options]
   196	 * @returns {string | null}
   197	 */
   198	export function guard(command, { isPath = () => false } = {}) {
   199	  // Where earlier `cd`s in the command moved to, relative to its start.
   200	  let dir = '.'
   201	  /** @type {IsPath} */
   202	  const fromDir = p => isPath(isAbsolute(p) ? p : join(dir, p))
   203	  for (const c of parseCommands(command)) {

content:
Delete the review engine and rename the plugin to trace
## Parent

#3

## What to build

Make the change easy: remove everything the decisions in #3 replace with existing skills, and rename the plugin to `trace`.

- Tag `quality-loop-v0.1.0` on the last commit that has the old code, and push the tag.
- Delete the review engine and everything that only serves it: the `review`, `improve`, `debug`, `full-send` and `tune-reviewer` skills, the four agents, the round step files, the CLI and its library modules, the eval runner, the old mod, and their tests.
- Keep only the destructive-git guard: its shell parser and destructive-command rules, and their table-driven tests. It is wired as the plugin's only hook.
- Rename the plugin to `trace` 0.2.0. It declares a dependency on `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`, and the marketplace allows that cross-marketplace dependency.
- Rewrite the root and plugin READMEs for the new purpose. Your preference for compacting at about 300k tokens becomes a README note pointing at Claude Code's own `autoCompactWindow` setting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The tag `quality-loop-v0.1.0` exists on origin and points at the last commit with the old code
- [ ] `npm run check` passes (typecheck, tests, plugin validation)
- [ ] `claude plugin validate` accepts the renamed plugin and the marketplace, dependency included
- [ ] In a live session with the plugin loaded, the guard refuses `git reset --hard` and `git push --force`
- [ ] No remaining file references the quality loop, except archived docs and the git tag
lolisaigao1234
## Progress: review rounds 1–2

**Commits:** 3b62dc7 (round 1 fixes), f5f8991 (round 2 fixes), on top of bfa09ae.

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] **Tag `quality-loop-v0.1.0`** created as an annotated tag on f164194 (`main`, the last commit with `plugins/quality-loop`) and pushed. `git ls-remote --tags origin` shows `refs/tags/quality-loop-v0.1.0^{}` → f164194.
- [ ] **`npm run check`**: typecheck and tests pass (128 tests). `npm run validate` could not run in this session because the `claude` CLI is not installed (`sh: 1: claude: not found`). **Still needs a human run.**
- [ ] **`claude plugin validate`** on the plugin and the marketplace: not run, same reason. The manifests follow the schema as far as I know it, but that is unverified.
- [ ] **Live session** (the guard refuses `git reset --hard` and `git push --force`): not done, because it needs a Claude Code session with `--plugin-dir plugins/trace`. The hook's own test drives `hook.mjs` with a PreToolUse payload and gets a `deny`.
- [x] **No references to the quality loop:** outside `archive/`, the only remaining mention is ADR 0005, which names the tag and the plugin it replaced. I left it as is: it is the decision record of the replacement, and the tag is the stated exception.

### Round 1: `/code-review` and `mattpocock-skills:code-review` against `main`
Fixed. These are all guard bypasses carried over from the old parser, each now covered by a case in the test table:
- **Brace-expansion blow-up** (`{a,b}` × 24 or more): the parse ran past the hook's 10s timeout, and a timed-out hook lets the command run. Expansion is now bounded.
- **Unquoted heredoc bodies** were treated as data, though their `$(...)` and backticks still run.
- **Heredocs piped into a shell** (`cat <<EOF | bash`, `<<EOF bash`) were treated as data.
- **`find -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir`:** the commands they run were not checked.
- **`$'...'` and `$"..."` quoting** was not decoded, so `$'git' reset --hard` got past the guard.
- **Pushes that delete remote refs** (`:ref`, `-d`/`--delete`, `--mirror`, `--prune`) were allowed.
- **`git stash -q drop`/`clear`:** an option before the subcommand hid it.
- **`git checkout <path>` without `--`:** it is now refused when the operand exists, which the hook checks against the filesystem from the session's `cwd` and `git -C`.

Standards fixes:
- Removed the dead `writes`/`xargs` fields left from the old guard. They were the Bash-write parsing that ADR 0007 rejects.
- Computed `shortFlags` once in the rm rule, and renamed `long` to `hasLong`.
- Each table case is now its own test.

Spec fix: the `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json` descriptions claimed tracing and forced reads, which have not shipped. They now say only the guard ships.

### Round 2: `/code-review` on the round-1 diff
Fixed:
- **What a shell reads is now a script, wherever it comes from:**
  - here-strings (`bash <<< '...'`);
  - `echo`/`printf` piped into a shell;
  - heredocs in any stage of the shell's pipeline, including a pipeline that continues after the body.

  Heredocs are tied to their own pipeline instead of their line. That also fixes a false deny when an unrelated `bash -c` was on the same line.
- **Brace alternatives past the 64-word cap** could hide a flag (`git reset {a0,…,a70,--hard}`). Every alternative now appears in at least one word.
- **`git checkout` of a glob, `:` pathspec magic or `--pathspec-from-file`** is refused. Paths are resolved after earlier `cd`s in the same command.
- **The timing test** allows 5s instead of 1s, so it won't be flaky on CI. Without the bound it would never finish.

### Decisions and answers given with a reason instead of a fix
- **`find -delete` is still allowed.** It would be a new rule. This ticket keeps the old rules, and the old guard denied it only for the loop's own state. It is the same class of judgement as `rm` without `-r`, which is allowed. **Question for the human:** add it as a follow-up?
- **`git checkout <name>` is refused when `<name>` is both a branch and an existing path** (for example a branch named `test` alongside a `test/` directory). The guard reads text and does not query git refs, so it fails closed. The deny message points to `git switch`.
- **The guard's deny does not name a pipeline step.** ADR 0006's rule is about trace hooks, and the guard is not a trace step.
- **`hook.mjs` fails open.** That is deliberate for the guard: a broken hook must not wedge the session. ADR 0007's fail-closed rule covers the forced-read hooks, which are not in this ticket.
- **The `<event>` dispatcher in `hook.mjs`** stays as the shared entry point for the hooks still to come under #3.
- **The guard is a seatbelt, not a sandbox** (README): scripts in files, aliases, and `cd` into variables can still get past it.

2	
3	This repository ships **trace**, a Claude Code plugin that keeps a model's work tied to the reason for it and to the project's decisions.
4	
5	## The trace
6	
7	**Trace**:
8	The chain of records that ties a change to its reason: an issue, its branch, its commits, its pull request, and the progress comments on the issue.
9	_Avoid_: audit trail, traceability chain
10	
11	**Pipeline step**:
12	One stage of producing a traced change. The steps are listed in ADR 0006.
13	_Avoid_: phase, stage
14	
15	**Traced repository**:
16	A repository whose owner has opted it in to the trace.
17	_Avoid_: enabled repo
18	
19	**Linked issue**:
20	The open issue that the current branch belongs to.
21	_Avoid_: current ticket
22	
23	**Ticket**:
24	An issue describing one vertical slice of work, under a parent issue.
25	_Avoid_: story
26	
27	**Parent issue**:
28	The issue that holds an effort's goal and decisions, whose tickets are its sub-issues.
29	_Avoid_: epic
30	
31	**Progress comment**:
32	A comment on the linked issue recording a round of work's progress, decisions and verification results.
33	_Avoid_: status update, round comment
34	
35	**Bypass**:
36	The human's switch for turning the trace off for a session.
37	_Avoid_: override, escape hatch
38	
39	## Doc authority
40	
41	**Related docs**:
42	The docs an agent must have read before it may change a file. Which docs these are is decided by ADR 0007, not by the agent.
43	_Avoid_: governing docs, authoritative docs, relevant docs
44	
45	**Full read**:
46	An agent's own read of every line of a file in its current form.
47	_Avoid_: skim, partial read
48	
49	**Stale read**:
50	A read of a file that has changed since it was read.
51	
52	**Active ADR**:
53	A decision record still in force.
54	
55	## Archive
56	
57	**Archive**:
58	The human's store of superseded docs, outside every agent's reach.
59	_Avoid_: attic, old docs, deprecated folder
60	
61	**Superseded**:
62	Replaced by a newer decision.
63	_Avoid_: deprecated, obsolete
64	
65	## Guardrails and view
66	
67	**Hard block**:
68	A refusal of an agent's tool call, which the agent cannot proceed past.
69	_Avoid_: warning, notice
70	
71	**Nudge**:
72	A hard block that applies once, and lets the next attempt through.
73	
74	**Guard**:
75	The hard block on commands that destroy work or history.
76	_Avoid_: safety hook, git guard
77	
78	**Archive block**:
79	The hard block on agents touching the archive.
80

82	The plugin's at-a-glance view of the trace.

1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0005: Reuse existing skills and Claude Code; the plugin is guardrails and visibility only
8	
9	The quality-loop plugin grew to about 8.7k lines of Node. Most of it reimplemented review, fix and debug loops that Matt Pocock's skills and Claude Code's own tools now provide; much of the rest defended the loop's own state against the model. We replace it with a plugin, `trace`, that adds only what no existing tool does: hooks that enforce the trace and doc authority (ADRs 0006–0008), the guard on commands that destroy work or history, and a mod that shows the trace: the band and a `/trace` command.
10	
11	The work itself goes through existing skills:
12	
13	| Need | Use |
14	|---|---|
15	| Plan, spec, tickets | Matt's `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets` |
16	| Build | Matt's `implement`, `tdd` |
17	| Debug | Matt's `diagnosing-bugs` |
18	| Review | Claude Code's `/code-review` for bugs; Matt's `code-review` for standards and drift from the issue |
19	| PR body | Matt's `pr` |
20	| Orchestration | Claude Code's Workflow tool, not custom agents |
21	
22	- `plugin.json` declares `mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official` as a dependency, so the reused skills are always present.
23	- The plugin ships two skills. `trace` is model-invokable and maps the pipeline onto the skills above. `setup` is user-only. Skills stay short: they steer a capable model and do not script it.
24	- When sources disagree, Matt's skills and the claude.dev posts win over TStack. Nothing more is taken from TStack.
25	
26	Supersedes the archived ADRs "A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong", "A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike", "A second model reviews through GitHub Copilot CLI, as one more lens" and "full-send takes a finished loop to a merged PR, and merges on green CI".
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	- The old code is deleted, not archived, and nothing shims it. The git tag `quality-loop-v0.1.0` marks its last commit; `trace` starts at 0.2.0.
31	- A review step that votes on findings, as the old loop did, comes back only as a plugin `workflows/` script, and only once Claude Code's `/code-review` proves too noisy.
32

content:
1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0006: Every change is traced through GitHub, and hooks enforce it
8	
9	A change that cannot be tied to the reason it was made is how drift and hallucinated work get in. In a traced repository, every change follows one pipeline, the **trace**:
10	
11	1. **Read**: the related docs (ADR 0007).
12	2. **Track**: an issue describes the change; tickets come from `to-tickets`.
13	3. **Branch**: `gh issue develop <n>` creates `<n>-<slug>` from the latest default branch, or from its blocker's branch while the blocker's PR awaits merge.
14	4. **Implement**: commits reference `#<n>`.
15	5. **Review**: a PR whose body says `Closes #<n>`.
16	6. **Update**: a progress comment on the issue after each round, giving progress, decisions and verification results.
17	7. **Close**: the human merges, and `Closes #<n>` closes the issue. Work that is not merged is closed with GitHub's state reason and a comment.
18	
19	Hooks hard-block, in the main session and in every subagent:
20	- an edit on the default branch;
21	- an edit on a branch whose `<n>-` names no open issue;
22	- `git commit` without `#<n>`;
23	- `gh pr create` without `Closes #<n>`.
24	
25	When commits were pushed after the issue's last comment, the Stop hook nudges for a progress comment: it blocks stopping once. Every deny names the pipeline step to go back to.
26	
27	The issue is also the record that survives compaction. At start, after compaction, on resume and when a subagent starts, hooks inject the issue's title, acceptance criteria and latest progress comment.
28	
29	## Considered options
30	
31	- **A local task file** (the old loop's approach): rejected. It is invisible to humans, dies with the worktree, and duplicates the issue.
32	- **Merge automation on green CI**: rejected. Merging is the human's decision.
33	- **Notices instead of blocks**: rejected. A model can ignore a notice; it cannot ignore a deny.
34	
35	## Consequences
36	
37	- The trace applies only in repositories opted in by `/trace:setup`, and only to files inside that repository's working tree. The archive block and the guard apply everywhere.
38	- The only bypass is an environment variable the human sets when launching Claude Code. Nothing the model can write turns the trace off, so there is no state to defend.
39	- Because the human merges, a ticket blocked by an unmerged one is built on a stacked branch.
40	- Repositories without a GitHub remote cannot be traced.
41

content:
1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0007: The related docs are forced reads, for every agent, before any edit
8	
9	Stale specs and invented terms enter when a model edits before it has read what the project already decided. Leaving the choice of what to read to the model means a relevant doc can be skipped. So the **related docs** are decided mechanically, and reading them is enforced:
10	
11	- `GLOSSARY.md`.
12	- The linked issue with its comments (`gh issue view <n> --comments`).
13	- Every active ADR in `docs/adr/`. An ADR may narrow itself with an `applies-to:` list of path globs in its frontmatter. It is then related only to edits of matching paths. An ADR without one is related to every edit.
14	- Every file under `docs/` that the issue body links.
15	
16	A doc counts as read only when the agent has read **the whole file itself**:
17	- Reads in chunks add up to the whole file.
18	- A partial view does not count.
19	- A read goes stale when the file's content changes after it.
20	- A subagent's reads are its own: its parent's context is not its context.
21	
22	A hard deny on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and on `git commit` as the backstop for changes made through Bash, lists exactly which docs are unread or stale. Where the hook's input is uncertain or undocumented, the check requires a re-read and never skips one.
23	
24	## Considered options
25	
26	- **The model chooses the relevant ADRs, with hooks only reminding it**: rejected by the user. A doc left to judgement is a doc that can be ignored.
27	- **Parsing every Bash command for writes**: rejected. That is what made the old guard 1,445 lines. The commit gate catches Bash-made changes before they land.
28	
29	## Consequences
30	
31	- Forced reads apply where the trace does: in traced repositories, to files inside the repository's working tree (ADR 0006).
32
