content:
1	---
2	status: accepted
3	date: 2026-10-28
4	issue: "#3"
5	---
6	
7	# 0008: Superseded docs live in a human-only archive that no agent can read
8	
9	A superseded ADR or doc in the model's context is a stale spec it may follow. Deleting it loses the human's record. So superseded docs move to `archive/` at the repository root, mirroring their original paths, each with a one-line "Superseded by ADR-NNNN" header. Active docs name an archived doc by title, never by link.
10	
11	The archive is managed by the human alone. Every model and agent, subagents and workflow agents included, is hard-denied:
12	- reading, searching or listing inside it;
13	- editing, writing or deleting there;
14	- moving or copying anything out of it;
15	- Bash commands that read a path inside it.
16	
17	Moving a file **into** the archive is allowed.
18	
19	Enforcement has two layers. The plugin's PreToolUse hook applies in every repository, because plugins cannot ship permission rules. In traced repositories, `/trace:setup` also adds Claude Code's own `Read(./archive/**)` deny rule to project settings.
20	
21	## Considered options
22	
23	- **A SubagentStart notice or injected context telling agents to stay out**: rejected. A notice is not enforcement; only a deny is.
24	
25	## Consequences
26	
27	- The hook reads command text. A search that reaches the archive without naming it, such as a repository-wide `rg`, must still be denied. Any route that cannot be closed is recorded here with the reason.
28	- That the hook fires for Workflow agents and Claude Code's `/code-review` fork is still to be verified. Until it is, those agents are not counted as covered.
29	- Code is never archived. Git history and tags keep it, and archived code would be exactly the context this exists to keep out.
30

Second review round on the guard:
- A shell's input is a script wherever it comes from: here-strings fed
  to it, echo/printf piped into it, and heredocs in any stage of its
  pipeline. Heredocs are tied to their own pipeline, not their line, so a
  shell elsewhere on the line no longer turns data into a script, and a
  pipeline that goes on after the body is treated as a script.
- Brace expansion keeps every alternative of every group in at least one
  word, so `{a0,...,a70,--hard}` cannot hide a flag past the cap.
- `git checkout` of a glob, `:` pathspec magic or --pathspec-from-file
  is refused, and paths are resolved after earlier `cd`s in the command.
- The timing test allows 5s: unbounded, it would never finish.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3b62dc7 Close guard bypasses found in review (#1)
- Brace expansion stops at its cap instead of expanding every
  alternative first, so `{a,b}{a,b}...` can no longer time the hook out
  (a timed-out hook lets the command run).
- Unquoted heredoc bodies have their $(...) and backticks checked, and a
  heredoc is a script whenever a shell on its line may read it
  (`cat <<EOF | bash`, `<<EOF bash`).
- Commands run by `find -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir` are checked.
- `$'...'` is decoded and `$"..."` reads as a double-quoted string.
- `git push` that deletes remote refs (`:ref`, -d/--delete, --mirror,
  --prune) is refused, as is `git stash <opts> drop|clear`.
- `git checkout <x>` is refused when x exists as a path, asked of the
  filesystem from the hook's cwd and any `git -C`.
- Drop the unused `writes`/`xargs` fields left from the old guard.
- Each table case is its own test; manifests describe only what ships.

[subagent] ## Standards

**Hard violations:** none that clearly break a rule. Commits reference `#1` (ADR 0006). The dead `writes`/`xargs` Bash-write parsing was removed, which matches what ADR 0007 rejects. No GLOSSARY _Avoid_ terms appear in the added lines.

**Borderline (rule wording):**
- `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json` both say "Guardrails for traced work." ADR 0006 (Consequences) says "the guard apply everywhere", not only in traced repositories, so the description narrows the Guard's scope wrongly.
- ADR 0006 says "Every deny names the pipeline step to go back to", and guard denies don't. The progress comment argues that rule covers trace hooks only. That reading is defensible, but the ADR doesn't say it.

**Judgement calls (Fowler):**
- **Duplicated Code.** Path resolution is written three times: `isAbsolute(b) ? b : join(a, b)` in `gitDestructive`, `isPath(isAbsolute(p) ? p : join(dir, p))` in `fromDir`, and `dir = isAbsolute(to) ? to : join(dir, to)` in the `cd` handling (guard.mjs).
- **Shotgun Surgery / tramp data.** `isPath` is passed through `guard → destructive → gitDestructive` only so the `checkout` case can use it. Each signature had to change.
- **Data Clumps.** `gitParts` now returns `{ config, dirs, sub, rest, opts, hasLong }`, and it grows by one field per review round.
- **Divergent Change.** `parseCommands`' `emit` now handles `-c` shells, `eval`, `find -exec` and here-strings, and `endPipeline` handles echo/printf. Every new bypass class means another edit to this one closure.
- **Primitive Obsession.** `endCommand(sep)` takes the string tags `'pipe' | 'end' | 'newline' | 'group'`, and `'group'` does nothing different from the others.

## Spec

Spec: *"Keep only the destructive-git guard: its shell parser and destructive-command rules, and their table-driven tests. It is wired as the plugin's only hook."*

**(a) Missing or broken:** nothing kept was lost. `npm test` passes 128 tests and `tsc` is clean. The guard is still the only hook. `npm run validate` and the live-session check are still unverified, as the progress comment admits, so two acceptance criteria stay open.

**(b) Scope creep.** These are fixes for bypasses of the kept rules: bounded brace expansion, unquoted heredoc substitutions, heredocs, here-strings and echo/printf piped to a shell, `find -exec`, `$'...'`/`$"..."`, and `git stash -q drop`. The following are new rules that the old guard at f164194 did not have (I checked its source):
- **Pushes that delete remote refs** (`:ref`, `-d/--delete`, `--mirror`, `--prune`). The old push rule only refused force and `+refspec`. The progress comment calls them "bypasses carried over from the old parser", which they aren't.
- **`git checkout <path>` with a single operand, a glob, `:` magic or `--pathspec-from-file`.** The old rule covered `--`, `.` and `<ref> <path>` only. This also adds filesystem I/O (`existsSync` from `cwd`) and `cd`/`-C` tracking to `hook.mjs`, which is new behaviour for a ticket that says "Keep only".

The agent declined `find -delete` because "It would be a new rule". That is the right test, but it wasn't applied to the two items above.

**(c) Implemented but wrong:**
- **The `cd` tracking leaks out of subshells and nested scripts, which bypasses the new checkout rule.** With `isPath = p => p === 'a.js'`:
  - `git checkout a.js` is denied.
  - `(cd /x); git checkout a.js`, `bash -c "cd /x"; git checkout a.js` and `echo $(cd /x); git checkout a.js` all return `null`, so they are allowed.

  The reverse happens too: `(cd src); git checkout a.js` is denied wrongly. The cause is that `guard()` advances `dir` for every `cd` that `parseCommands` emits, including ones from `(...)`, `$(...)` and `bash -c`.
- **Branch/path ambiguity fails closed.** `git checkout test` is refused whenever a `test/` directory exists. This is documented, but it changes ordinary branch switching, which goes past "keep".
- **Not covered by the new pipe handling:** `cat file | bash` is still allowed. This is consistent with "seatbelt", but the README now lists piped input as checked without that caveat.

3	Hooks that keep a model's work traced and its context grounded in the project's decisions (ADRs 0005–0008). It depends on `mattpocock-skills`, which supplies the skills the work goes through.

6	
7	A PreToolUse hook on Bash. In every repository, and in every subagent, it refuses commands that destroy work or history:
8

10	- force pushes, including `+refspec`, and pushes that delete remote refs (`:ref`, `--delete`, `--mirror`, `--prune`)

12	- `--no-verify`, `commit -n`, and overriding `core.hooksPath`
13	- `rm -r`

Commands inside `bash -c`, `$(...)`, backticks, `find -exec` and `xargs` are checked, and so is what a shell reads: heredocs and here-strings fed to it, and `echo`/`printf` piped into it. So are the substitutions in unquoted heredocs, and `$'...'` quoting is decoded. It reads command text, so it is a seatbelt, not a sandbox.
